title: Crossing the Rope Bridge
story:
Jonas and his friend Aisha were hiking toward a mountain hut. A fast stream blocked the trail, and the water looked cold. The only way across was a rope bridge of boards and thick cords. Aisha read a notice nailed to the first post. It said one person should cross at a time and hold both ropes.

Jonas waited on the bank while Aisha tested the first board. The cords felt rough under her hands. The bridge swayed, and she kept her eyes on her shoes. She did not look down at the white water. On the far side, she turned and called that the boards felt firm. Jonas stepped on and moved slowly, board by board. Halfway across, a board creaked, so he shifted his weight. He took a breath and continued to the last post. Aisha grabbed his sleeve and helped him onto solid ground. They both laughed with relief and drank some water.

Before they left, they checked the bridge for loose cords. Everything looked strong. Later, they wrote a short note in the hut book. The note told the next hikers to cross one by one. That evening, the hut keeper thanked them for the clear warning. He said a storm was coming, and careful people would need the news. Jonas and Aisha ate soup and felt proud of the crossing.
